It's a really good game. Very pleasant graphics, satisfying combat action, nice attention to details, fantastic setting and story. It gets a bit repetitive at 20-30 hours mark, and I found just a few really powerful builds personally, a lot of the upgrades you get feel really bad compared to some really powerful ones. Flames with crit chance is probably the best weapon out there to spam attacks and win, but you get really depressed when you spend 10 changes of fate for a single boon to give you some juicy attack damage and you get some shitty upgrades for sprint, special or cast every time you spin it.

Everything you liked about Hades and a lot more. Some people said they liked the story less, but I found it even more engaging. 

At first all the new weapon aspects and arcana cards and elements make it seem a bit daunting, but you will catch on eventually. So many play styles makes for a lot of replay value and rewards experimentaiton.
So far this is a great example of how to do a sequel. All the parts of the first game that hooked me are still there, they added more but kept the theme and spirit of the original.

100+ hrs gameplay and I must say. I enjoyed this more than Hades 1. Don't get me wrong, the simplicity and straightforward-ness of Hades 1 is the reason I got hooked to this genre. But man oh man, Hades 2 got me playing so hard. I really recommend this. A real time eater!

Great gameplay n progression, average story, poor immersion/dialogue, disturbing(temporarily) themes.

MY ISSUE WITH STORY AS A SUMMARY WITHOUT SPOILERS:
Main character, a pseudo child soldier, latches onto an empty raison d'être and aims to do things MUCH worse than the villain she targets in order to save people with similar levels of villainy.

How am i supposed to feel good about winning?

...Post Finishing the story:
Ok, the ending wasnt grimdark but getting there without some story incentive was a bit of a slog.
fun game even while in early review but can get repetetive when youve defeated all the current bosses
After finishing the game and reaching the end (?), I can confidently say its even better than the first one. Definitely worth the money. Everything fades, family stays.

what never fails to amaze me is how many wildly different builds there are, yet every run still feels both familiar and unique. it totally captures my short attention span. i love Hades, and i loved this game even more. i can never thank Supergiant Games enough!

Even in early access I have had a great time playing this game. Combat feels good overall, though I feel there are some areas where it can be improved (the skull as a weapon doesn't thrill me, and I feel there are enemies that are too punishing). I find Melinoe's hero's journey really compelling and the game's themes of transformation intriguing. I cannot wait for the story to be finished as I am really interested in what has yet to be revealed. 8.5/10 overall right now!

After 100 hours in, I can honestly say that Hades II is not only a great successor to one of the best roguelikes ever made - it’s actually even better.

The number of possible builds and weapons that completely change the way you play is outstanding (I’ve already lost count of how many new “favorite” builds I’ve had…). And the best part is that you’re constantly discovering something new! The pace at which new mechanics and content are introduced is extremely well designed - really, folks from Supergiant mastered this art in their games. Lastly, just like in Hades, the sheer amount of content is impressive. I’m more than 100 runs in and still unlocking new dialogue lines or prophecies.

If you’re new to the series, Hades might be more beginner-friendly, but you can absolutely start here without missing out. It’s pure fun!

Side note: Steam Deck performance is top-notch. No tweaking needed.

I didn't think I'd like a roguelike as much as I grew to absolutely love this. I did play Hades in 2025 but it didn't really click with me back then, and I decided to try this one now and oh boy am I loving it. Banger story, banger characters, amazing execution. Just all around very very good. One of the best roguelikes I have ever played and I am loving it.

I would recommend this if you liked the first game. The gameplay is different enough to feel interesting and there is already a lot of content despite being in early access. Now that the game is fully released, the game is even better!

Cool game, great art. Fantastic. It's still in early access, not as good as the first one mostly because I don't like most of the new weapons and it takes time to get the one's that I find more interesting.
Great game, I imagine the basic game will be much better!

Really struggled to get into the dash spam nature of the first one but really enjoy the weighty feel of the second one. If you enjoyed the concept of the first and happen to be open to a slight change in the combat mechanics this is a 10/10 recommendation.
Amazing game, just wow! These developers know exactly what the players want. Big applaud, really. Thank you

I last played this game over a year ago until very recently. They have changed so much over the course of the year, and what they've added is great. This game continues to improve and is so worth the $30.

if you enjoyed the first game, this game is very similar in terms of combat mechanics and relationships. it isn't just a copy+paste of Hades I, as this game adds in some new mechanics of its own as well

The music, the gameplay, the art design all as good as the first game even for an early access it's already so impressive. I enjoy that the game is hard bc its a rouge like still buggy here and there but definitely can't wait to see the game be fully fleshed out.

This game is wonderful, and the story is a perfect sequel to the first game, but also works well as its own standalone game! I have been playing it since the early access first released and it is SO worth it! I cannot wait to experience the finished product!!!!

I will always and forever recommend SuperGiant Games. Story is great, gameplay is great and the Art Style will far outlast every "realistic" and graphically intense games.
20 out of 10

Great game. Feels similar to the first Hades but different. It first i didn't love the new feel but it grew on me. The game is still in EA which makes it really fun to pick back up and play after each update to see how the game has improved. I'm really excited to be apart of EA, it's already a great game.

Even in it's beta stages it has (much like it's predecessor) felt more like a complete game than a lot of AAA titles at release. I honestly can't praise the developer enough for the series incredible art direction, solid game-play and overall engaging stories and characters.

That is as much as I'll say for my review cause I don't really want to spoil anything. But if you enjoyed the first Hades, then this is a no-brainer. Like for real.... why haven't you bought this yet? Just click on that buy button. Go on. I'm waiting.

And if you haven't experienced Hades yet (but enjoy/think you'd enjoy good action rogue-likes), then just go buy the first game. That way, you'll have this wonderful sequel to fall back on when you'll inevitably want more.

The learning curve is very real, but once you get the hang of controls and mechanics, it’s a fantastic time. It’s a huge exercise of self-control to not keep playing until I’ve unlocked everything that’s available.

I'm definitely biased, but I prefer the storyline of Hades 1. That's not to say that the plot of this game isn't brilliant. Especially since it contains a LOT of references to The Odyssey and epics that come after. It was great going through it all, unlocking conversations and lore as I went. I can also say that while I think Hades 1 has amazing gameplay already, Hades 2 improved on perfection. The new weapon mechanics, boons, and side quests are massively entertaining and fun to adapt to.
Amazing game, it is not yet finished but has enough content to be bought. Different enough from original Hades to be worth playing. Different enough gameplay from original Hades to be worth playing

Superb. Fixes basically all of my gameplay gripes from Hades 1 and polishes every other aspect that was already great. Easy pickup if you loved the first game, and highly recommended if you enjoyed Hades but wanted more depth and variety in the combat specifically.

is Hades 2 good ? should you buy it now ? the first answer is yes its great from the art to the feeling of the game its fantastic. the second answer is no not unless you know its not in a release state right now and your fine with waiting for content. if your a super fan and want to support the devs like me then buy the game and have fun with whats here.

It's everything that the first one is and more. In a world where games are constantly released half finished, this game was basically done when it entered Early Access. There are virtually no bugs, everything almost always works as intended, and the incredibly important one: the animations are actually accurate to where the hit box is, every time. No visual lag, no being hit by phantom attacks or things you're well outside of, and no attacks that use the exact color palette of the background. It is such a massive breath of fresh air to see a game release that has some actual thought and care put in to every aspect of it.

I completed Night's Champion and every weapon testament, and I've nearly 100% everything the game has to offer (at high fear too) and I still love it. It's a breath of fresh air in the absolute slog of mediocrity and sloppy half-games we get on the regular. 

This game has something for everyone, even if you don't think you're a rogue-like fan. You should play it.

Hades was an incredible game, I loved it despite in general not liking Rogue Likes. In many way Hades 2 is better, the combat the tighter, there are more options and there is more game. It is brilliant.

The story is also excellent however it does lack some of the charm of the original Hades' story. It's much larger "Scale" means at times it can feel a little less tight and this is especially true in the epilogue, when some of the RNG quest trigger elements begin to get a tad frustrating.

Overall Hades 2 is a fantastic game, well worth your time. It might not quiet live up to the Original as a story but as a game it is a distinct improvement.
I couldn’t have asked for a better sequel, it enhances every element that made the first game so great. Pure, endless fun!!

A stellar game with so much unique dialogue to go along with the wide variations of upgrades, it has a deep well of curated content of fans looking for something more from their roguelike.
I'm not sure why I got this since I didn't care for the first game, but I'm glad I did! Very addicting gameplay and solid sense of progression.

One of, if not, THE MOST addictive game I've ever played. This game took over my life for the better part of two months. The gameplay loop is always fresh, where failure is no setback, but progress in the story and dialogue between characters. If you're a fan of roguelikes, this is a MUST play. The world feels alive, characters react to the smallest actions you do, it's like the game is observing you and you feel like you're part of the world, and not just an outsider in the eyes of the NPCs. Honestly, do yourself a favor, and pick this up and enjoy hundreds of hours of never ending fun.

I bought this game less than two weeks ago.
...
I've unlocked every aspect of every weapon. I cried at this game, and rage quit more than once. I have never played a better game, and may not again. 
If you're debating getting it or not, just do it. I promise you won't regret it.

This game has a grand feel to it. The gods waging war against Chronos makes me very engaged in the storytelling. The zones are a bit less diverse in terms of environment than in the first game, but since there is more zones in this one I don't mind too much. 

The gameplay is the strongest part of this game. Its hard to stop playing sometimes!

The game has a lot more stuff (bosses, systems, voicelines etc.) than the first one yet I never enjoyed it quite as much due to the gameplay changes. Then I got to the ending.
The ending is so genuinely rushed and bad it ruined my desire to go any further. Pretty much all story threads either end abruptly, go nowhere or are completely unbelievable to the point I thought it was a fake-out and surely the real ending would start soon.
Visuals are gorgeous, music is much more diverse and easy to listen to than the first game's and the voice acting is good and plentiful all of which couldn't save the game for me.
Played it since Early Access and still now after the full release. Good game, very fun. I recommend if you like roguelikes or Hades.

This is already amazing in Early Access, I can't wait to see and play it once its fully released. It's just as much a labor of love as the first title, and it's just as much (if not even more) fun. There already is a ton of content, and Supergiant isn't even done yet.

The artwork, story, soundtrack, and voice acting are amazing. The new weapons and abilities (compared to the first game) are a breath of fresh air, and it feels both same-and-new, in a good sense.

If you're on the fence about this: buy the game. I promise it's worth it.

I played this since I played Hades 1 and I loved it. There are old characters that you get to talk to again alongside new characters so the game doesn't feel like a repeat. It had be guessing what would come next in the story line which is something I enjoy a lot in games. I love how the art style is still similar to hades 1. but also completely different. It is such a good sequel. It has new aspects like the surface and the underworld, and other mechanics like how you fight, that make the game feel very different from the origonal, in a good way. Overall really loved this game and am excited to see what else the story has in store for me.
Everything from the the gameplay to the art style oozes with passion. One of the best rogue likes ive ever played.

After clocking in over 40 hours in Hades II's early access, I can confidently say: this game delivers. It’s everything I loved about the original Hades—and somehow, it’s even more addictive, ambitious, and refined.

At its core, Hades II expands on the formula that made the first game a masterpiece. The combat is fast, fluid, and endlessly satisfying, with a whole new layer of depth thanks to fresh weapons, mechanics, and boons. The first couple of hours felt like learning to walk again—I was stumbling through the new systems, unfamiliar enemies, and pacing—but once it clicked, I couldn’t put it down. There’s a hypnotic rhythm to it: experimenting with builds, mastering new playstyles, and feeling yourself improve with every run.

Even in early access, the game feels rich and polished. The storytelling, voice acting, and art are already top-notch, and it’s clear Supergiant poured a ton of heart into every detail. The characters are compelling, the world is mysterious and mythic in all the right ways, and the loop of combat, progression, and discovery is as addictive as ever.

If you loved the first Hades, this sequel is a no-brainer. Highly recommended.

Proudly followed this game from early access and to see it grow from a game worthy of the first game into a game that stands above it is epic. Hades II is the best rouge like ever made. Play the masterpiece original first, then dive into the epic sequel.
One of the most faithful sequels i have ever played. I am happy to have played this and even be part of the beta test early on. Please make another hades game supergiant
